who: Historian of Africa at Howard University, 1976–2011; PhD in African history, University of Birmingham, 1972.

evidence.says: The AHA identifies Aziz Batran as Howard history faculty from 1976 to 2011 and records his Birmingham PhD in African history in 1972.
The authority for Aziz A. Batran cites Islam and Revolution in Africa (1984), identifying its author as a Howard history professor with a Birmingham doctorate.

notes: The authority and AHA biography identify the same Howard African historian, in post during Mbughuni’s doctorate.

who: Professor of Latin language and literature at Université Laval; supervisor in ancient studies.

evidence.says: Under 2011, Laval lists Laurent Gohary’s Interregnum doctorate in ancient studies with Alban Baudou as director.
The authority cites À l’école de Virgile (2015), whose cover identifies Alban Baudou as professor of Latin language and literature at Université Laval.

notes: Direct student, title, university and year match; the authority supplies the same faculty affiliation.

who: John W. Bicknell, Drew University scholar of Victorian literature and editor of Leslie Stephen’s letters.

evidence.says: The authority identifies John W. Bicknell through Selected Letters of Leslie Stephen (1996) and an MLA notice naming Drew University.
Drew University Archives lists John W. Bicknell as acting graduate dean, 1967–1969.
Drew’s faculty/alumni bibliography lists John W. Bicknell’s publications on Victorian literature.

notes: Drew affiliation and work on Leslie Stephen distinguish this candidate from the other Bicknell records. Stenfors’s individual supervision was not independently documented.

who: Casimir C. Gecys, scholar of Soviet studies at Fordham University in the 1960s; author of Two Worlds (1964).

evidence.says: Language and Area Study Programs in American Universities (1964), printed page 105, lists Casimir C. Gecys among Fordham’s Institute of Contemporary Russian Studies faculty, with religion and philosophy as his fields.
The Casimir C. Gecys authority identifies him as the author of Two Worlds (1964).
Southern Illinois University’s George S. Counts papers catalogue records Casimir C. Gecys’s Two Worlds, issued by Fordham’s Institute of Contemporary Russian Studies in 1964.

notes: The authority’s work connects to the same Fordham institute where the contemporary directory lists Gecys, close to Gromada’s 1966 doctorate.

who: Historian of Parisian social history at Université Laval; history faculty from 1972 to 2005 and subsequently professor emerita.

evidence.says: Laval records Christine Piette’s history appointment in 1972, retirement in 2005, doctoral supervision and research on Parisian social history; it lists emerita recognition in 2008.

The Christine Piette authority cites Les Juifs de Paris (1808–1840) and Les Parisiennes au travail au milieu du XIXe siècle; the latter identifies her as professor emerita in Laval’s historical sciences department.

notes: Exact name, department and research field agree. The Christian Piette candidate is not the matching record; Munch’s individual supervision was not independently documented.

who: Medieval art historian at Université Laval, teaching in its history department from 1960 to 1997 and subsequently professor emeritus.

evidence.says: Laval identifies Roland Sanfaçon as professor emeritus who taught medieval art in its history department, 1960–1997, and researched stained glass and flamboyant architecture.
The authority’s citation to Chinese-English-French kuaisu dictionary (1997) identifies Roland Sanfaçon as a professor of art history at Laval University.
Claire Labrecque’s article on the Saint-Esprit chapel at Rue identifies her Laval affiliation and states in note 3 that her doctorate on the chapel is directed by Roland Sanfaçon.

notes: Labrecque’s own published article directly confirms supervision on the same monument; the authority matches his Laval art-history post.

who: Scholar of ancient scripture and ancient history at Brigham Young University; doctorate from the University of California, Berkeley.

evidence.says: The authority identifies C. Wilfred Griggs as BYU ancient-scripture faculty with a Berkeley doctorate in a 1984 source, and as BYU ancient-studies faculty in a 1993 source.
BYU’s Religious Studies Center describes Wilfred Griggs of BYU directing its Egyptian excavation project beginning in 1981 and cites publications under C. Wilfred Griggs.

notes: Exact name, BYU appointment on both sides of 1990 and ancient-history field agree. Bailey’s individual supervision was not independently documented.

who: Historian of science at Université du Québec à Montréal from 1987; first director of CIRST in 1992.

evidence.says: CIRST identifies Camille Limoges as a historian who joined UQAM in 1987 and became its first director in 1992.
The authority connects Camille Limoges to UQAM teaching from 1987 and to the CIRST director profile, and records a Sorbonne PhD in 1968.
The CIRST bulletin, volume 6, number 2 (summer 2002), reports Nicolas Marchand’s doctorate on the history of Canadian psychologists, co-supervised by Camille Limoges and Yves Gingras.

notes: Institution, field and direct confirmation of Marchand’s co-supervision establish identity. The AHA completion year was not independently reconciled with the later bulletin announcement.
